title: Five ways to switch and sunset SystemSketch previews
brief: Generalize the current Stable → Preview action into named development presets that can open stock tldraw plus one feature, small feature variants on the product UI, or larger compositions—then retire previews without weakening the immutable Stable escape hatch.
defaultWhy: Preset Shelf is the provisional default at 95.6/100. It gives Zach the low-cognitive-load preset model he is reaching for, makes lifecycle state visible, and maps onto the current one-Stable-server + one-live-Preview-server design without inventing another runtime per preset.
decisionHinge: The recommendation depends on whether this is primarily a human switching surface or an agent/reproducibility protocol. If shareable URLs and source-controlled definitions become more important than browsing and lifecycle visibility, V5 Manifest Router should supply the substrate—or replace the visible shelf entirely.
invariants: The ordinary app entry remains the immutable verified Stable safety anchor.
All development presets reuse one live Preview/Vite server; presets do not create codebases or ports.
Every Preview opens an independent board snapshot or read-only view; Stable and Preview never autosave the same real .tldr file.
Composition is selected before the tldraw editor mounts, because registered shapes, tools, and schema are construction-time capabilities.
Preset selection and lifecycle metadata live outside .tldr document content.
boundary: Standalone interactive UI/architecture prototypes using the same Robot sorter.tldr scenario. Switching, story controls, picks, and lifecycle state are real inside the gallery; no launcher endpoint, preset registry, profile composition, clone creation, or production SystemSketch UI has been implemented.

requirements.name: Focused one-step switching
requirements.why: The point is to isolate one subassembly without dragging volatile UI or unrelated work back into attention.
requirements.passCondition: From Stable, Zach can identify and open Block Dev as stock tldraw + Block in one obvious action without reconstructing its configuration.

anchors.1: Requires remembering flags, rebuilding a configuration, or navigating several unrelated controls.
anchors.3: The target is reachable but the choice or its consequences require interpretation.
anchors.5: The named target and what it includes are immediately legible and open in one action.

requirements.name: Composition range without conceptual lies
requirements.why: The system should support isolated features and small variants on the full UI, while keeping build, composition, and document policy distinct.
requirements.passCondition: The model can represent stock + Block, product shell + Block variant, and larger recipes without pretending each is a release or separate server.

anchors.1: Supports one special-case Preview only or conflates release and composition.
anchors.3: Supports common named recipes but makes novel combinations awkward.
anchors.5: Represents arbitrary valid compositions while keeping build and document policy explicit.

requirements.name: Safety boundary stays unmistakable
requirements.why: A feature-preview mechanism is useful only if broken work cannot strand or silently overwrite the real working document.
requirements.passCondition: Stable remains visibly immutable and every experimental target visibly opens an independent duplicate on the live working tree.

anchors.1: The user can plausibly mistake a composition for Stable or create competing writers.
anchors.3: The safety policy exists but is revealed late or inconsistently.
anchors.5: Channel, composition, and document ownership are visible before launch and remain visible afterward.

requirements.name: Clean sunset and historical clarity
requirements.why: Temporary previews should disappear from the active surface without breaking links silently or turning the selector into an attic.
requirements.passCondition: Block Dev can be retired in one understandable action; active lists stay clean and an old reference explains what replaced it or that it is gone.

anchors.1: Retirement means an unexplained 404, stale menu item, or manual cleanup in several places.
anchors.3: The preview can be hidden or deleted, but old references and replacement paths are weak.
anchors.5: Active, archived, successor, and eventual removal states are explicit and low-maintenance.

requirements.name: Fit with the current implementation
requirements.why: SystemSketch already has one Stable server, one live Vite Preview, snapshot handoff, launch URLs, and a quiet Help/update surface.
requirements.passCondition: The proposal extends those seams with a small preset registry and URL parameter rather than replacing the release architecture.

anchors.1: Requires new processes, duplicated builds, or a broad launcher rewrite.
anchors.3: Reuses the core but adds significant new state or coordination machinery.
anchors.5: Adds a small declarative registry and routes through the existing clone/launch transaction.

hardGates.name: Stable remains the ordinary immutable entry
hardGates.why: A preset system must never weaken the recovery anchor.

hardGates.name: No two writers on one .tldr
hardGates.why: Every experimental launch must preserve the existing independent-copy safety rule.

hardGates.name: Composition is document-neutral
hardGates.why: Choosing or sunsetting a preset must not mutate board content; registered capabilities are chosen before mount.

variants.name: Preset Shelf
variants.thesis: Treat each useful build + composition + document policy as one named launch recipe in a small human-readable catalog.
variants.bestWhen: Zach usually wants a known working context—Block Dev, Rows Lab, Full Preview—without rebuilding its ingredients.
variants.losesWhen: Novel ad-hoc combinations are more common than recurring presets, or automation is the only consumer.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A named preset whose details expand to build, shell, capabilities, and document policy.

decisions.label: Launch
decisions.value: One click snapshots the Stable board and opens the preset on the existing Preview server.

decisions.label: Sunset
decisions.value: Archive hides it from Active, preserves old URLs with a successor for one release, then removal is safe.

proof: The hero opens on the same Stable Robot sorter.tldr context and makes Block Dev legible as stock + Block + independent copy.
The direct Sunset action moves Block Dev out of the active shelf and leaves an archived successor notice.

fr1.evidence: Block Dev is a named card with its exact composition and a single Open action; no axes must be reconstructed.

fr2.evidence: Any valid recipe can be named, but novel combinations require creating another preset or dropping to an advanced surface.

fr3.evidence: The current Stable anchor and Block Dev's Live working tree + independent copy policy are visible together before launch.

fr4.evidence: The exercised state change removes the card from Active while retaining an archived row and successor explanation.

fr5.evidence: The card can compile to the existing previewClone + launch URL transaction and needs only a small recipe registry.

g1.evidence: Stable remains the fixed first card and is not editable from the shelf.

g2.evidence: Every development card explicitly launches an independent copy.

g3.evidence: Recipe selection is launcher state and all capability labels are resolved before the preview editor mounts.

variants.name: Build × Composition Matrix
variants.thesis: Expose the real dimensions directly: choose a build row, a composition column, and let the selected cell define the launch target.
variants.bestWhen: Zach regularly compares the same composition across Stable and live work, and wants invalid combinations made explicit.
variants.losesWhen: The goal is focused feature work; a Cartesian grid makes simple named jobs feel like configuration.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A coordinate in build × composition space rather than a named bundle.

decisions.label: Launch
decisions.value: Selecting a valid cell previews its exact build and feature registration before opening.

decisions.label: Sunset
decisions.value: Retire a composition column; historical builds retain disabled cells rather than active menu entries.

proof: The matrix distinguishes verified Stable from the live working tree and product, stock, Block, and Rows compositions.
The Sunset interaction disables the Block column and identifies Rows as its successor.

fr1.evidence: Block Dev is visible, but the user must interpret a row/column coordinate and disabled cells before launching.

fr2.evidence: Build and composition remain genuinely orthogonal and every valid combination has an explicit cell.

fr3.evidence: Rows make build identity clear and Preview cells say copy, though the dense grid can still blur the primary safe path.

fr4.evidence: A column can be disabled, but retirement leaves historical/invalid cells and needs explanation in several places.

fr5.evidence: The underlying launch can reuse current seams, but the matrix and validity logic add state beyond a small preset registry.

g1.evidence: Stable is a fixed build row; unavailable feature compositions are disabled, not synthesized.

g2.evidence: All live-row launches display Copy before opening.

g3.evidence: The cell resolves a composition before mount and never writes the board.

variants.name: Ephemeral Preview Sessions
variants.thesis: Treat previews as temporary running experiments that expire automatically unless Zach pins them.
variants.bestWhen: Many short-lived agent experiments are opened and the main problem is accumulated preview clutter.
variants.losesWhen: The same named contexts should remain durable muscle-memory targets across weeks or releases.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A launched session with preset, source fingerprint, board copy, last-used time, and TTL.

decisions.label: Launch
decisions.value: Start from a small template list; the session then becomes the thing managed.

decisions.label: Sunset
decisions.value: Unpinned sessions expire after a quiet period; pinning promotes one to a durable preset.

proof: The hero shows Stable separately from three live sessions with explicit board copies and expiry clocks.
The direct interaction expires Block Dev and leaves a recoverable Recently ended row.

fr1.evidence: Starting a known session is simple, but the surface is organized around running instances rather than reusable feature intent.

fr2.evidence: Any session may carry a recipe, but comparing or creating compositions is secondary to lifecycle management.

fr3.evidence: Every session card names its source fingerprint and independent board copy while Stable stays separate.

fr4.evidence: TTL makes sunset automatic, pinning is explicit, and the exercised ended state is recoverable without cluttering Active.

fr5.evidence: It can reuse the launcher but adds session persistence, TTL evaluation, pinning, and cleanup machinery.

g1.evidence: Stable is a separate always-present anchor outside session expiry.

g2.evidence: Each session names its unique Untitled preview copy.

g3.evidence: Expiry and pin state belong to session metadata, not tldraw records.

variants.name: Capability Stack Composer
variants.thesis: Build a preview by stacking independently registered capabilities, then optionally save that exact stack as a named preset.
variants.bestWhen: The design space itself is under investigation and Zach frequently needs combinations nobody anticipated enough to name.
variants.losesWhen: The main need is focused work on a few recurring contexts; the composer invites tinkering and choice overhead.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: An ordered stack: base shell + capability layers + optional UI layer.

decisions.label: Launch
decisions.value: Validate the stack, name it if useful, then open the resolved recipe on a cloned Preview board.

decisions.label: Sunset
decisions.value: Delete or archive only the saved recipe; reusable capability modules remain available to other stacks.

proof: The hero starts at Stock + Block and directly adds Product shell to produce a small-feature-on-existing-UI composition.
The supporting exhibit separates recipe retirement from capability-module removal.

fr1.evidence: Block Dev can be reproduced, but the primary surface asks Zach to manipulate ingredients rather than select a known job.

fr2.evidence: The ordered layer model directly represents isolated tests, full UI variants, and novel combinations with validation.

fr3.evidence: The resolved recipe can show live build and clone policy, but the flexible composer makes the safe default less dominant.

fr4.evidence: Recipes can disappear cleanly while modules survive, though old recipe URLs still need tombstone handling elsewhere.

fr5.evidence: A capability dependency graph, compatibility validator, ordering rules, and composer UI exceed the current small launch seam.

g1.evidence: Stable is not a composable layer; the workbench always targets Live Preview.

g2.evidence: Launch summary fixes document policy to Independent copy.

g3.evidence: The stack is resolved and validated before constructing the editor and is stored outside .tldr.

variants.name: Manifest Router
variants.thesis: Make presets source-controlled route descriptors first; humans and agents reach them through URLs or a command palette rather than permanent chrome.
variants.bestWhen: Agents create most previews, reproducible links matter, and Zach prefers the main canvas to stay visually quiet.
variants.losesWhen: Zach wants to browse what exists, compare several options visually, or manage lifecycle without remembering commands.

decisions.label: Primary object
decisions.value: A versioned manifest record with stable ID, resolved profile, status, and optional successor.

decisions.label: Launch
decisions.value: Command palette or `?preset=block-dev` resolves the descriptor and routes through the current clone launcher.

decisions.label: Sunset
decisions.value: Change status to archived and add `replacedBy`; old URLs render a tombstone instead of silently drifting.

proof: The hero uses a realistic command palette over the current canvas and shows the complete Block Dev route summary.
The direct Sunset state keeps the old command/URL resolvable but redirects intent to Rows Lab.

fr1.evidence: A searched Block Dev command opens in one action, but the available set is less glanceable than a persistent shelf.

fr2.evidence: Manifests can encode arbitrary validated recipes, but authoring new combinations happens in data/code rather than direct UI.

fr3.evidence: The route summary explicitly states Live working tree and independent copy, while Stable remains outside preset resolution.

fr4.evidence: Archived status and replacedBy keep old links honest, though the lifecycle is less visible without invoking the palette or opening the URL.

fr5.evidence: A typed descriptor and query parameter fit the existing launchUrl and previewClone seams with minimal permanent UI.

g1.evidence: Preset manifests resolve only on the Preview channel; the ordinary icon still opens Stable.

g2.evidence: The command summary fixes board policy to Independent copy before launch.

g3.evidence: The manifest is resolved before React selects the profile and never becomes board data.

steps.caption: The same ID becomes an honest tombstone that points to Rows Lab instead of breaking or silently changing meaning.
